title: Medical Records Request (Release of Information): Request Types, Requesters and Authorization Matrix
content:
Riverbend Regional Health's Health Information Management (HIM) department handles every Medical Records Request (Release of Information) as one of seven request types. The request type fixes who may file the request, the basis on which it is filed, and whether a signed authorization or a signed written direction must stand behind it.

## Who may file each request type, and on what basis

| Request type | Who may file it | Basis of the request |
|---|---|---|
| Patient Access - Electronic Copy | the patient or a personal representative | HIPAA right of access, electronic copy of electronic records |
| Patient Access - Paper Copy | the patient or a personal representative | HIPAA right of access, paper copy |
| Patient-Directed Transmission to a Third Party | the patient or a personal representative | signed written direction naming the recipient |
| Authorized Release - Attorney or Legal Representative | an attorney | valid HIPAA authorization signed by the patient |
| Authorized Release - Insurer or Disability Carrier | an insurer or disability carrier | valid HIPAA authorization signed by the patient |
| Amendment of Health Record Request | the patient or a personal representative | written amendment request with a reason |
| Accounting of Disclosures Request | the patient or a personal representative | written request for an accounting |

## Authorization, written direction and identity, by request type

Column meanings:

- **Patient's HIPAA authorization required**: whether a valid HIPAA authorization signed by the patient is required.
- **Signed written direction required**: whether a signed written direction naming the recipient is required.
- **Authorization age limit**: the number of calendar days after the patient's signature during which an authorization is accepted, unless the authorization states an earlier expiration.
- **Identity verified before release**: whether the requester's identity is verified before release.

| Request type | Patient's HIPAA authorization required | Signed written direction required | Authorization age limit (calendar days) | Identity verified before release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Patient Access - Electronic Copy | No | No | 0 | Yes |
| Patient Access - Paper Copy | No | No | 0 | Yes |
| Patient-Directed Transmission to a Third Party | No | Yes | 0 | Yes |
| Authorized Release - Attorney or Legal Representative | Yes | No | 180 | Yes |
| Authorized Release - Insurer or Disability Carrier | Yes | No | 180 | Yes |
| Amendment of Health Record Request | No | No | 0 | Yes |
| Accounting of Disclosures Request | No | No | 0 | Yes |

## Entries that are the same for every request type

The following entries hold identically for all seven request types of the Medical Records Request (Release of Information) product — Patient Access - Electronic Copy, Patient Access - Paper Copy, Patient-Directed Transmission to a Third Party, Authorized Release - Attorney or Legal Representative, Authorized Release - Insurer or Disability Carrier, Amendment of Health Record Request and Accounting of Disclosures Request:

| Entry | Value for every request type |
|---|---|
| Documents accepted as proof of personal representative status | an activated health care power of attorney; a guardianship order; letters of administration |
| Record classes that need a specific consent beyond a general authorization | substance use disorder records protected under Part 2; HIV test results; outpatient mental health treatment records |
| Routing for subpoenas and court orders | Riverbend Legal Services |

## Reading the matrix

- An attorney's request and an insurer's or disability carrier's request are the two request types that rest on the patient's signed HIPAA authorization, and both carry an authorization age limit of 180 calendar days after the patient's signature, unless the authorization states an earlier expiration.
- A Patient-Directed Transmission to a Third Party is the one request type that rests on the patient's signed written direction naming the recipient; it does not call for a HIPAA authorization.
- Identity verification before release is marked "Yes" on every request type, whoever the requester is.
- A personal representative's status is proved with one of the three documents listed above; the same three documents serve for every request type.
